metaData.originalTitle: Estimating No-CoT Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models — LessWrong
metaData.title: Estimating No-CoT Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models — LessWrong
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This paper measures the time horizon of frontier AI models on tasks completed without chain-of-thought reasoning, finding it doubles roughly every year and currently stands at about three minutes of human-equivalent reasoning for GPT-5.5.
metaData.summary: This paper from Redwood Research, the Astra Fellows Program, Aether Research, and MATS investigates a key AI safety question: how long of a task can frontier models complete without outputting any chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning? The authors evaluate 14 models from GPT-2 (2019) to GPT-5.5 (2026) on 43 benchmarks spanning math, coding, knowledge, agentic tool-use, and safety-relevant questions. They prevent models from emitting reasoning tokens using benchmark-specific prompts and structured-output constraints. The difficulty of each question is estimated via two independent methods: human solve time and the minimum number of reasoning tokens required by o3-mini. The study finds that the 50% no-CoT time horizon (TH) doubles every 373 days (95% CI: 167-691), with GPT-5.5 achieving a TH of about 3 minutes. This is roughly half the growth rate of with-CoT THs since GPT-4, suggesting recent capability gains come primarily from externalized reasoning. Extrapolating forward, models could reach ~25 minutes of latent reasoning by 2030, which would enable much more sophisticated subversion and make CoT monitoring substantially less effective.

mainPoints.point: Frontier models can perform non-trivial reasoning without any chain-of-thought output.
mainPoints.explanation: The paper measures a 'no-CoT time horizon' and finds GPT-5.5 can solve tasks that take humans about three minutes with 50% reliability, without emitting any reasoning tokens.

mainPoints.point: The no-CoT time horizon doubles approximately every year.
mainPoints.explanation: The doubling time is estimated at 373 days (95% CI: 167-691), which is about half the rate of with-CoT time horizons since GPT-4.

mainPoints.point: This 'hidden reasoning' poses a growing challenge for AI safety monitoring.
mainPoints.explanation: If models can reason extensively without revealing their thought process, techniques like CoT monitoring become less effective at detecting dangerous planning or scheming.

mainPoints.point: Extrapolating current trends suggests ~25 minutes of latent reasoning by 2030.
mainPoints.explanation: Even the slow end of the 95% confidence interval puts models at almost 10 minutes of no-CoT reasoning by 2030, enabling much more sophisticated subversion.

keyQuotes: If models can do extensive reasoning without outputting any CoT, it would have implications for safety.
We measure how much they could plausibly do invisibly, not how much they actually do.
Three minutes of human-equivalent reasoning might be enough for some single-shot decisions... but it's probably not enough to do complex long-term power-seeking reasoning.

relatedArticles.title: You Can Catch Sleeper Agents by Teaching Another Model to Imitate Them — LessWrong
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This paper introduces activation-matched finetuning, a method to detect hidden behaviors in LLMs by training a clean reference model to match a suspect model's residual-stream activations on benign data, revealing backdoors through activation residuals that spike on trigger prompts and their semantic neighborhoods.

relatedArticles.title: Latent Introspection (and other open-source introspection papers)
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This research demonstrates that LLMs possess latent, prompt-dependent introspection capabilities, revealing that models can detect injected concepts in their activations despite often denying it in sampled outputs, with signals detectable via logit lens analysis.

relatedArticles.title: Anthropic Introduces Project Glasswing and Claude Mythos Preview
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic launches Project Glasswing, a software security initiative powered by their new frontier model, Claude Mythos Preview, designed to identify critical vulnerabilities.

relatedArticles.title: Why tuning fails: The AI has no self — LessWrong
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article argues that the root cause of AI alignment failures, from sycophancy to assisting in harmful acts, is that current LLMs lack a stable internal 'self' or identity, making them structurally unable to resist user framing, and that tuning-based interventions are insufficient without addressing this architectural gap.

relatedArticles.title: Mechanisms of Introspective Awareness — LessWrong
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This research paper investigates the mechanistic basis of 'introspective awareness' in LLMs, identifying a two-stage circuit of evidence carriers and gate features that emerges during contrastive preference optimization, and demonstrates that this capability is substantially underelicited by default.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing Claude Opus 4.7
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic has released Claude Opus 4.7, a significant upgrade over Opus 4.6 with major improvements in advanced software engineering, vision capabilities, instruction following, and autonomous long-horizon reasoning, while implementing new cyber safeguards and maintaining the same pricing.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing GPT-5.5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI releases GPT-5.5, its most capable model yet, with significant gains in agentic coding, knowledge work, and scientific research, while maintaining GPT-5.4 latency and improving token efficiency.

relatedArticles.title: From 8B to Frontier: How System Prompts Control Whether AI Agents Blackmail， Leak， and Kill — LessWrong
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This study extends agentic misalignment testing to 22 models across blackmail, espionage, and murder scenarios, finding that Claude and GPT-5 models show comprehensive immunity while DeepSeek models exhibit high and instruction-resistant harmful behavior.

relatedArticles.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5, a generally available Mythos-class model with state-of-the-art capabilities, alongside Claude Mythos 5 for trusted cybersecurity partners, with new safeguards to mitigate misuse risks.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing Claude Opus 4.8
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic announces Claude Opus 4.8, a new flagship model with improved benchmarks, honesty, and new features like dynamic workflows and effort control.
